question: What creates the suction power in a manual vacuum aspiration system?
explanation: The MVA system utilizes a specialized handheld syringe that the operator pulls to generate negative pressure before beginning the evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Why is manual vacuum aspiration preferred over electric pumps in many rural Nigerian clinics?

options.A: It allows multiple providers to operate it at once
options.B: It does not require electricity to operate
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for local anesthesia
options.D: It can remove pregnancies of any gestational age

explanation: The reliance on manual suction makes MVA independent of electrical power grids, ensuring reliability in resource-limited settings. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: What is the maximum gestational age typically recommended for performing manual vacuum aspiration?
explanation: MVA is safely indicated for uterine evacuation up to 14 weeks of pregnancy, after which alternative surgical methods are required. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: A patient with an acute pelvic infection presents for uterine evacuation. Why is MVA contraindicated?

options.A: It can spread bacteria deeper into the pelvic organs
options.B: Infection neutralizes the local anesthetic drugs
options.C: Negative pressure will fail to create a seal
options.D: The plastic cannula will melt in infected tissue

explanation: Performing instrumentation in the presence of untreated pelvic inflammatory disease risks driving pathogens upward into the fallopian tubes and peritoneal cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: What is the typical fluid capacity of a standard MVA vacuum aspirator cylinder?
explanation: Standard MVA aspirators hold 60 cubic centimeters of volume, which helps clinicians measure the volume of evacuated products of conception. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What is the purpose of applying a small amount of silicone oil to the piston of the MVA syringe?

options.A: To numb the internal rubber components against friction heat
options.B: To maintain an airtight seal and ensure smooth movement
options.C: To sterilize the internal parts before the procedure starts
options.D: To prevent the plastic cannula from clogging with tissue

explanation: Silicone lubrication keeps the rubber piston gliding easily against the cylinder wall while preserving the vacuum pressure needed for aspiration. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why must a patient empty her bladder immediately before undergoing manual vacuum aspiration?

options.A: To ensure the speculum stays locked in the correct position
options.B: To prevent uterine displacement and minimize discomfort
options.C: To collect a sterile urine sample for routine malaria testing
options.D: To prevent the local anesthetic from wearing off too quickly

explanation: An empty bladder allows the uterus to rest in its natural position, making bimanual examination and safe cannula insertion much easier. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for MVA expresses intense fear about surgical pain and complications. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative immediately without getting her verbal feedback
options.B: Provide calm reassurance, explain the steps clearly, and discuss pain relief options
options.C: Tell the patient that worrying will only make the bleeding much heavier
options.D: Reschedule the procedure for another day without offering any explanation

explanation: Active listening, clear education, and reassurance effectively reduce patient anxiety and build trust before clinical procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: Which instrument is used to gently grasp and stabilize the cervix during an MVA procedure?
explanation: A tenaculum is clamped onto the anterior lip of the cervix to straighten the uterocervical angle and stabilize the tissue during instrument entry. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What clinical sign indicates that the uterine cavity has been completely evacuated during MVA?

options.A: The vacuum syringe plunger automatically pushes itself down
options.B: Blood starts bubbling rapidly through the clear plastic tubing
options.C: Red or pink foam appears in the cannula without solid tissue
options.D: The patient reports severe lower abdominal cramping pain

explanation: The appearance of gritty tissue stopping, the uterus contracting tightly around the cannula, and foamy red fluid signal complete evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of floating evacuated uterine tissue in a water basin?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of blood lost during surgery
options.B: To dissolve blood clots so the tissue can be discarded safely
options.C: To wash away toxic bacteria before laboratory testing
options.D: To confirm the presence of products of conception

explanation: Floating the specimen helps the nurse or doctor clearly identify chorionic villi or gestational tissue, confirming a complete uterine evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Why is contraceptive counseling provided immediately following an MVA procedure?

options.A: Ovulation and fertility can return within two weeks
options.B: The uterus will prolapse if another pregnancy occurs too soon
options.C: Hormonal pills are required to stop post-operative bleeding
options.D: Local clinic policy mandates permanent birth control use

explanation: Because a woman can become pregnant again very quickly after uterine evacuation, starting contraception before discharge prevents rapid repeat pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: A patient complains of severe, sharp abdominal pain and dizziness shortly after an MVA procedure. What complication is most likely occurring?
explanation: Severe, worsening abdominal pain and signs of internal bleeding or shock following instrumentation strongly suggest that the uterine wall has been breached. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: Which medication is commonly administered immediately to manage postpartum or post-abortion uterine hemorrhage caused by atony?
explanation: Oxytocin stimulates strong uterine contractions, compressing blood vessels in the myometrium to control bleeding effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What is the recommended concentration of chlorine solution used for immediate instrument decontamination after MVA?
explanation: A 0.5% chlorine solution is standard for decontaminating surgical instruments and inactivating bloodborne viruses like HIV and hepatitis before washing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: Why must MVA cannulae and syringes be washed with soap and water before undergoing final sterilization?

options.A: Detergent prevents the silicone lubricant from evaporating away
options.B: Soap adds a pleasant fragrance that reassures the next surgical patient
options.C: Organic matter protects microorganisms from heat or chemical sterilization
options.D: Water activates the plastic hardening agents inside the tubing walls

explanation: Blood and tissue proteins can shield bacteria and spores during autoclaving or chemical disinfection, making thorough cleaning mandatory. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)
